intended_object: The linear dual M^* = Hom_R(M, R) of a finitely generated projective module M over a commutative ring R, seen as an object of the full subcategory of finitely generated projective R-modules. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module (the monoidal / rigid structure on finite projective modules).
explanation:
I read the definition and the library's `finiteProjectiveModules` in `TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/CartanMap/Basic.lean`. That object property is `Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Projective R M` on `ModuleCat R`. The definition takes the underlying module to be `ModuleCat.of R (Module.Dual R M.obj)`, which is exactly Hom_R(M, R). The membership proof uses Mathlib's instances saying that the dual of a finite projective module is again finite and projective, so the object is the standard dual.

Generality is natural. `R` is an arbitrary commutative ring, which the dual needs in order to be an R-module. The construction is the dual inside this specific full subcategory, so it makes sense to state it there. Mathlib's `Module.Dual` provides the underlying construction; this definition only packages it as an object of the subcategory. It does not duplicate a more general Mathlib notion at narrower generality.
